I did not deploy v2.3.2 and did not open the incident.

**Why:** v2.3.2 has no release record for checkout-api at all, so it has never been healthy in production. Policy requires change-manager approval before deploying a version in that state. I have no way to record that approval through my tools, and the deploy tool doesn't take an approval field, so I stopped instead of deploying.

**Current state of checkout-api:**
- Production (us-east, us-west, eu-west) is running **v2.3.1**, which is marked unhealthy with a **0.18 error rate**.
- The last known healthy production release is **v2.3.0**.
- v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy (staging).

**I did not open the SEV3 incident.** You asked for it to record the change after the deploy, and no deploy happened, so an incident now would document a change that isn't live. Opening it would also page the on-call engineer.

**Next steps, if you want to proceed:**
1. Get change-manager approval for v2.3.2 and send it to me. I can then deploy and open the SEV3 incident.
2. Or tell me to roll production back to v2.3.0, which is the last healthy version. The 0.18 error rate on v2.3.1 is a live problem and may need attention regardless of the hotfix. I can also open an incident for it if you want the on-call engineer involved.
